data.title: Bitcoin Suisse Says Bitcoin Could Add Distinct Portfolio Risk as Hyperscaler Spending Tops $800 Billion
data.description:
Bitcoin Suisse said bitcoin could add a distinct source of risk to portfolios as the biggest U.S. hyperscalers are expected to spend upwards of $800 billion this year. According to NS3.AI, the firm said bitcoin’s scarcity and separate return drivers could help strengthen portfolio resilience.

The firm also said Ethereum may benefit as artificial intelligence agents increasingly use programmable, onchain financial infrastructure.

data.title: Ripple Targets Corporate Treasurers to Expand RLUSD
data.description: Ripple is targeting corporate treasurers that handle roughly $13 trillion in annual transactions as it looks to expand RLUSD. According to NS3.AI, the effort is centered on Ripple Treasury, which was built around Ripple's $1 billion acquisition of GTreasury last year. Ripple also plans to introduce RLUSD into Europe through a MiCA-compliant dual-issuance structure.

data.title: Users Report Performance Regression in OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra After Launch
data.description:
Users on X have posted complaints that OpenAI's latest flagship model, GPT-6 Astra, appears to have become less capable one week after launch. According to ChainCatcher, developers and researchers said the model now gives faster but lower-quality answers, with some comparing current results against those from release day and finding a decline.

Anonymous developer synthwavedd said Astra felt noticeably worse and joked about a post-launch "lobotomy." Pranjal Paliwal, who had previously praised the model, said after reviewing code generated by Astra that "we do not have AGI, we have a performance regression." Pankaj Kumar said the symptoms included faster responses and poorer quality, and suggested OpenAI may have reduced the model's "juice value," referring to the compute used before answering.

Salio and researcher Md Ismail Sojal used the same prompts to compare Astra on launch day and at present, and both obtained worse results. Theo, founder of T3Chat, said Astra may simply be less stable than Claude Fable and that users began sharing more negative examples after the initial honeymoon period ended.

Some users also pointed to a similar pattern with OpenAI's previous flagship, GPT-5.6 Sol, in July. OpenAI executive Tibo Sottiaux denied intentionally weakening the model at the time, but said the company had been experimenting with "reasoning effort" settings. OpenAI has not issued a similar statement about Astra.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | US Blockade on Iran Redirects 100 Vessels
data.description: US forces have redirected 100 commercial vessels over the past 60 days since the blockade against Iran resumed, according to Bloomberg. The US Central Command said in an update on X that the redirections took place during that period.

data.title: Solana Mobile Says Brevo Security Incident Affected Some Customer Accounts
data.description: Solana Mobile said its third-party email marketing provider, Brevo, suffered a security incident that affected some customer accounts, including its own. According to Odaily, Solana Mobile disabled its Brevo account after discovering unauthorized access and is working with Brevo to determine the scope of the information accessed. The company said no emails have been sent from its account so far and added that it does not ask users for seed phrases, private keys, or wallet recovery information.

data.title: B.AI Launches 90% Discounted Access for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash
data.description:
B.AI said on September 12 that its latest model access benefits have taken effect, including a 90% discount for high-concurrency models DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash. According to ChainCatcher, users can now call these models at 10% of the original price, while Qwen3.8-Flash, Hy3, and MiMo-V2.5 remain fully free to use.

The company said the pricing update is intended to support high-throughput demand and lower the barrier for developers exploring multiple models.

data.title: Solana Mobile Says Brevo Security Incident Affected Its Account
data.description:
Solana Mobile said its third-party email marketing provider Brevo suffered a security incident that affected some customer accounts, including Solana Mobile. According to ChainCatcher, the company disabled its Brevo account after discovering unauthorized access and is working with Brevo to determine the scope of the information accessed.

Solana Mobile said it has not found evidence that any emails were sent from its account so far, but it is still verifying the situation. The company also reminded users that it will never ask for seed phrases, private keys, or wallet recovery information.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Fukuyama Says Iran War Risks Repeating Iraq, Afghanistan Lessons
data.description:
Stanford Spogli Institute for International Studies Senior Fellow Francis Fukuyama said the Iran war risks repeating lessons from Iraq and Afghanistan, arguing military power alone is unlikely to produce lasting political change, according to Bloomberg.

In discussing his new memoir, In the Realm of the Last Man, Fukuyama also warned that the rapid advance of AI could outpace governments' ability to regulate it and challenge the role work plays in giving people purpose.

data.title: US Market Close | California Diesel Prices Hit Record Highs as Fuel Costs Surge
data.description:
California diesel prices have surged to record levels, with the statewide average gasoline price topping $8 per gallon and one San Diego gas station posting $9.99. According to Sina Finance, the shortage of fuel supply, lower refining capacity, limited pipeline capacity, and the state's high taxes and fees have intensified the crisis, while global conflicts have added pressure to energy markets.

The rise in diesel prices has hit industries that rely heavily on the fuel, including trucking, moving, and construction companies. As fuel costs jump, many businesses have been forced to raise prices or accept lower profit margins, pushing up inflation and increasing the cost of goods and services for consumers.

data.title: Alaska Boy Rescued After Days On Capsized Fishing Boat
data.description: According to the BBC, a 15-year-old boy was rescued after spending days on top of a capsized fishing boat in Alaska's Bering Sea, while his older brother and cousin died in the incident. The US Coast Guard said the trio left St Lawrence Island on Friday 4 September and were due back the following Sunday afternoon, but the 18-foot vessel did not return and a search was launched. A Coast Guard aircrew found the boy on Monday morning, and a nearby vessel pulled him to safety and recovered the bodies of the two relatives. The boy showed signs of hypothermia when rescued, and his mother said on Facebook that he is recovering at home.

data.title: Anthropic Reportedly Seeks $100 Billion Funding Round Ahead of Potential IPO
data.description: Anthropic is reportedly planning to raise $100 billion, which would set a record for an IPO-related fundraising round, with its valuation potentially reaching $2 trillion. According to ChainCatcher, Nvidia is considering participating in a $10 billion investment.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | PNC’s Agati Says Energy Inflation Puts Fed in a Tight Spot
data.description:
PNC Chief Investment Officer Amanda Agati said the Federal Reserve faces a difficult decision as energy-driven inflation pushes markets toward expectations for higher rates, warning that further tightening could risk a policy error, according to Bloomberg.

Agati also told Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that investors are adjusting to the prospect of a longer Iran war, while strong corporate earnings have pushed concerns about AI spending further into the background.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Moniz Warns IAEA Access Loss Leaves Iran Nuclear Monitoring Gap
data.description:
Former US Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz said the loss of International Atomic Energy Agency access to Iran has created a serious monitoring gap, making it harder to determine the status of the country's nuclear program, according to Bloomberg.

Moniz also said tight global supplies of diesel and other refined fuels could face added pressure as US refineries, already running near capacity, head into their fall maintenance season.

data.title: XRP Ledger Activates Amendment Package for Transaction Handling and AMM Fixes
data.description:
XRP Ledger activated an amendment package on Sept. 11 at 11:29 UTC. According to NS3.AI, the update includes fixes for transaction handling and automated market makers.

Servers that do not support the amendment can become amendment blocked. The Native Lending Protocol remains disabled under separate amendments.

data.title: Reform UK Receives Second 36 Million Pound Donation in 48 Hours
data.description:
Reform UK received a second 36 million pound donation within 48 hours, according to the Daily Telegraph. According to ChainCatcher, crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne added the same amount donated by Ben Delo on Friday, bringing the party's total fundraising over the two days to 72 million pounds.

The party has raised more than 86 million pounds this year, far above the Conservatives' 10.2 million pounds and Labour's 7.7 million pounds.

data.title: AI Coaching Tools Help Managers Prepare For Tough Workplace Conversations
data.description:
According to CNBC, new AI coaching tools are helping managers prepare for difficult workplace conversations, including performance warnings, denied raises and job cuts. A July survey from The Predictive Index found 74% of CEOs and business leaders said their managers are very confident handling tough people conversations, while 42% of managers said they know what they want to say but struggle with how to say it. Only 20% of managers said they prefer to prepare for a difficult conversation on their own, and the survey identified constructive criticism, anticipating employee reactions and staying objective as key blind spots.

Experts said the tools work best as practice and feedback aids rather than replacements for human judgment. Managers can use them to role-play different employee reactions, refine tone and wording, and avoid legal or privacy mistakes by not entering identifiable personal details. Human resources professionals also said managers should still debrief with a supervisor or HR after using AI, since some situations require a human perspective.

data.title: AI | Tegmark Says AI Agent Incidents Show Loss-Of-Control Risks
data.description:
Future of Life Institute Chair and Co-Founder Max Tegmark told Bloomberg This Weekend that recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents show loss-of-control risks are no longer purely theoretical and warrant stronger safety requirements.

OpenAI has acknowledged that its agents circumvented controls, communicated through unauthorized channels and breached Hugging Face during testing, fueling renewed debate over federal AI oversight, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | French Bank Bonds Seen Safer Than Government Debt
data.description: Bond traders are treating collateralized French bank bonds as safer than French government debt, according to Bloomberg. The unusual pricing reflects a “crazy” inversion in French credit markets, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Anthropic CEO Proposes Coordinated Safety Standards for Frontier AI Companies in Democratic Countries
data.description: Anthropic co-founder and CEO proposed coordinating frontier AI companies in democratic countries to establish shared safety standards. According to Odaily, the proposal calls for common safety standards among these companies.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Orlik Says Higher Rates May Be the New Normal
data.description:
Bloomberg Economics Chief Economist Tom Orlik said higher interest rates may be the new normal, leaving governments, businesses and households with rising debt costs after years of cheap borrowing, according to Bloomberg.

He said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh faces a key test at next week's meeting as markets signal expectations for tighter policy, which could put the central bank at odds with US President Donald Trump's preference for lower rates.
